Role Models of Malaysia

Inspiring Figures

Discover national figures whose leadership, vision, and dedication have shaped Malaysia's progress across government, culture, tourism, and society.

Contribution Highlights

  • Introduced national development policies
  • Strengthened rural economy
  • Laid foundation for modernization

PRIME MINISTER


Tun Abdul Razak

11 March 1922 Second Prime Minister of Malaysia

Tun Abdul Razak is widely regarded as the “Father of Development” in Malaysia. Serving as the nation’s second Prime Minister, he introduced significant economic and rural development programs that transformed Malaysia’s socio-economic landscape.

His New Economic Policy aimed to reduce poverty and restructure society, laying the foundation for Malaysia’s modernization and long-term stability.

Contribution Highlights

  • Promoted Malaysian cuisine globally
  • Preserved traditional cooking heritage
  • Cultural ambassador in culinary events

CULINER


Chef Wan (Datuk)

6 January 1958 Culinary Ambassador of Malaysia

Datuk Chef Wan is one of Malaysia’s most celebrated culinary figures. Known for his vibrant personality and dedication to preserving traditional Malaysian cuisine, he has introduced Malaysian flavors to international audiences through television programs, cookbooks, and global food events.

He actively promotes authentic recipes while modernizing presentation styles, ensuring that Malaysian cuisine continues to evolve without losing its cultural roots.

Contribution Highlights

  • Advocates governance reform
  • Promotes unity and inclusive development
  • Influential voice in Malaysian politics

POLITIC


Anwar Ibrahim

10 August 1947 National Political Leader

Anwar Ibrahim is a prominent Malaysian political figure known for his advocacy of reform, social justice, and economic development. Throughout his political career, he has played a significant role in shaping Malaysia’s democratic framework and governance structure.

His leadership emphasizes unity, transparency, and progressive policies aimed at strengthening Malaysia’s global competitiveness.

Contribution Highlights

  • Revolutionized low-cost aviation in Asia
  • Promoted regional tourism growth
  • Recognized global business leader

HOTEL


Tony Fernandes

30 April 1964 Entrepreneur & Aviation Industry Leader

Tony Fernandes is a Malaysian entrepreneur best known for transforming AirAsia into one of Asia’s leading low-cost airlines. His visionary leadership revolutionized affordable air travel, making flying accessible to millions across Southeast Asia.

Contribution Highlights

  • Led independence negotiations with Britain
  • First Prime Minister of Malaysia
  • Promoted multiracial political cooperation

ACCOUNTING

Tunku Abdul Rahman

30 April 1964 First Prime Minister of Malaysia

Tunku Abdul Rahman was a central figure in Malaysia’s journey toward independence and is widely recognized as the Father of Independence. Born on 8 February 1903 in Kedah, he was educated in both Malaya and the United Kingdom, including at the University of Cambridge.
